The maximum value of OM + ON − MN is 1 + √3 − √(2√3) ≈ 0.871.

**Setup.** Place O at the origin with OX along the positive x-axis. Then P = (√3/2, 1/2). Let M = (a, 0) and N = (0, b). Triangle OMN has a right angle at O, so its inradius r satisfies

OM + ON − MN = a + b − √(a² + b²) = 2r.

The task is therefore to maximize the inradius r of triangle OMN over lines through P.

**Incircle condition.** The incircle has center (r, r) and radius r, and it is tangent to the line MN with the circle on the origin side of that line. Since P lies on line MN, P cannot lie strictly inside the incircle. This requires

(√3/2 − r)² + (1/2 − r)² ≥ r².

**Boundary case.** Expanding, the boundary is

3/4 − √3 r + r² + 1/4 − r + r² = r²,

which simplifies to r² − (√3 + 1)r + 1 = 0. Its roots are

r = [(√3 + 1) ± √(2√3)] / 2.

P lies outside the disk for r at most the smaller root, so the maximum r is the smaller root. At the larger root (about 2.30), the tangent line at P would have the circle on the far side from O, so the circle would be an excircle, not the incircle. That root is rejected.

**Result.** The maximum of r is r = [(√3 + 1) − √(2√3)] / 2 ≈ 0.4355. It is attained when line MN is tangent to the incircle at P. Hence

2r = 1 + √3 − √(2√3) ≈ 0.871.

ANSWER: $1+\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}}$
